title: Operation Sindoor Commander Named First CEO of Ayodhya Ram Temple Trust
excerpt: Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra, selected from over 5,500 applicants, takes charge of the Ram Janmabhoomi Trust as it seeks to restore credibility after a donations embezzlement scandal.
body:
• Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra has been appointed the first CEO of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, selected from 5,585 applicants after a two-month screening process.
  • Mishra commanded the Indian Air Force's Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor and received the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal on Independence Day 2025.
  • The appointment comes amid controversy over alleged embezzlement of temple donations that led to eight arrests and the resignation of General Secretary Champat Rai.
  • Three new trustees — Mahesh Bhagchandka, Madan Mohan Pandey, and Dr. Nirmala Yadav — were also inducted at the same meeting.

The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has appointed retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as its first-ever Chief Executive Officer, tapping one of India's most decorated military leaders to lead a sweeping institutional overhaul at the Ayodhya temple complex.

The decision was announced on Wednesday following a meeting of the Trust's trustees in Ayodhya. Mishra, who commanded the Indian Air Force's Western Air Command during last year's Operation Sindoor, was selected from a pool of 5,585 applicants through a two-month process that included online screening, 111 video interviews, and 16 in-person interviews in Ayodhya.

A Military Career Spanning Four Decades

Mishra brings 38 years of distinguished service in the Indian Air Force to the role. Commissioned into the fighter stream on December 6, 1986, he is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, the Air Force Academy, and the U.S. Air Command and Staff College in Montgomery, Alabama. He also attended the Royal College of Defence Studies in the United Kingdom.

Over his career, Mishra logged more than 3,000 flying hours across 18 types of fighter and transport aircraft. He served as Chief Test Pilot at the Aircraft and Systems Testing Establishment, commanded a fighter squadron and two frontline air bases, and rose to become Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Air Command — one of the IAF's most strategically critical posts.

His most recent military distinction, the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal, was awarded on Independence Day 2025 for his leadership during Operation Sindoor. He had earlier received the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2024 and the Vishisht Seva Medal in 2013.

"After 43 years of national service, this appointment feels like a blessing. My focus will be on building systems, procedures, and operational practices aligned with the nature and scale of the organization."

— Air Marshal (Retd.) Jeetendra Mishra

Restoring Trust After Scandal

The appointment comes at a critical juncture for the Ram Temple Trust, which has been embroiled in controversy over alleged siphoning of donations. Eight people were arrested in connection with the embezzlement probe, and Champat Rai, the Trust's former General Secretary who oversaw the temple's construction, resigned amid the scandal.

The Trust has said the CEO will function independently without government interference and report to its General Secretary. Mishra is expected to formulate long-term plans for temple and donations management, establishing the kind of institutional governance the Trust has lacked since the temple's consecration in January 2024.

Beyond the CEO appointment, the Trust inducted three new members: Delhi-based Mahesh Bhagchandka, Ayodhya-based Madan Mohan Pandey, and Shikohabad-based Dr. Nirmala Yadav. Swami Govind Dev Giri was elevated to General Secretary. The restructuring represents the most significant administrative overhaul of the Trust since the temple opened.

Reactions and Significance

The Vishva Hindu Parishad welcomed the appointment. VHP International President Alok Kumar praised Mishra's credentials, citing his service record during Operation Sindoor and his decades of administrative experience in defense. However, prominent Ayodhya seers objected to the three new trustee appointments, arguing the inductees lacked roots in the historic Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

For the Indian diaspora, the Ram Temple holds deep cultural and religious significance. Overseas donations constituted a meaningful share of the temple's construction fund, and the appointment of a professionally credentialed CEO signals the Trust's intent to bring transparency and institutional rigor to an organization that has global stakeholders.
